results.title: Nvidia Warns Hyperscalers Its AI Server Prices Are Jumping More Than 15% - Startup Fortune
results.author: Elroy Fernandes
highlights:
## The Bill Is Reaching Renters

The pain is already showing up further down the chain. Nebius raised on-demand GPU rental prices by roughly 30% from June 1, with H100 pricing moving from $2.95 to $3.85 per GPU-hour and B200 pricing from $5.50 to $7.15, according to pricing notices tracked by market reports. Amazon followed with an increase of about 20% to EC2 Capacity Block pricing for machine-learning GPU instances from July 1, as Investing.com reported from AWS pricing documentation. Those increases came before the latest round of anxiety over memory costs. That tells you this isn't a one-time shock.

results.title: ISSUE #7: The B300 Trickle
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
Published Aug 25, 2026 

 Weekly Cloud Pricing Pulse, week ending August 24, 2026: the floor held, and an established chip is still finding its public price 

 Published August 25, 2026 · Pricing evidence through August 24, 2026 · Ornn Compute Price Index (OCPI) through August 23, 2026, 20:00 UTC. 

 The LinkedIn edition of the AIForge Works Weekly Cloud Pricing Pulse: one read on public GPU cloud pricing across nine providers, every week. 

 The one-line read. The four public floors did not move this week: H100 SXM $3.85, H200 $4.29, B200 $6.69, A100 SXM4 $2.30, the same levels we have shown since mid-July. Two things moved around them. The OCPI transaction index rose under three of the four floors, narrowing every gap on the board. And the B300, a chip that has been shipping since last year, is still finding a public price: only a few clouds list it on-demand, intermittently, and where they do the numbers range from about $7.85 to about $26.15 per GPU-hour. A settled floor, a firming index underneath it, and an established Blackwell GPU whose public price is still a trickle. 

## This week 

- Floors held. All four board floors are unchanged: H100 SXM $3.85 (Nebius), H200 $4.29 (Crusoe), B200 $6.69 (Lambda), A100 SXM4 $2.30 (Crusoe), the same levels we have published since mid-July. Across all nine indexed providers, no comparable public on-demand rate moved more than 1% week over week.
- The index moved under them. The floors held, but the OCPI transaction index did not. Week over week it rose for H100 ($2.64 to $2.87), B200 ($5.93 to $6.64), and A100 SXM4 ($1.02 to $1.07), and fell for H200 ($4.75 to $4.42). With the floors flat, every gap on the board narrowed. B200’s floor is now just $0.05 above the index, the tightest spread on the board.
- The B300 trickle. The B300 is an established Blackwell-generation GPU, in market since last year, with prior history in the AIForge Works catalog. What is still catching up is its public price. Only a handful of clouds list it on-demand, and they do so intermittently: AWS’s eight-GPU p6-b300.48xlarge appeared in Seoul for the first time in our reviewed history this week (Linux and four licensed operating-system variants), while Nebius listings dropped and then returned. We now see publicly listed on-demand B300 rates from three providers, AWS, OCI, and Nebius; CoreWeave shows the SKU but its rate is still contact-sales. The listed rates disagree sharply, from about $7.85 per GPU-hour (Nebius, three regions) to about $26.15 (AWS, Seoul). That is catalog visibility, not orderable capacity, and it is what a chip still finding its public price looks like.

...

What changed this week is underneath: three of the four index values rose toward the floor, so the board’s spreads are the narrowest we have shown. Read the board as a reference gap, not a quote. These are the lowest indexed public catalog rates, which is not the same as orderable, in stock, or inclusive of negotiated terms.

...

The public catalog rates AIForge Works presents are on-demand and normalized to a per-GPU-hour basis unless stated otherwise. OCPI is transaction-index context, not a catalog price. Listed or indexed does not mean orderable, and neither is a live quote, an availability guarantee, or a purchase recommendation. Verify current pricing, availability, terms, and fees directly with the provider before acting.

results.title: GPU Clouds Compared: Nebius on Price, CoreWeave at 3AM | THE D*AI*LY BRIEF
results.author: Rajesh Beri
highlights:
Normalised to one workload: 64 NVIDIA B200 GPUs — eight nodes of eight, InfiniBand-connected, running continuously for 30 days. That is 46,080 GPU-hours. No spot, no preemption, no partial-node fractions. The neocloud prices below were read off each vendor's live pricing page on 30 August 2026; the AWS, Azure and Google Cloud rates come from outside trackers, because those vendors do not publish a simple per-GPU-hour rate. Treat the Google row with the most caution: it is the one number here sourced to a rival GPU cloud's blog rather than a neutral tracker, and it is worth knowing that before it is used to call Google expensive.

...

| Provider | Tier | B200 $/GPU-hr | 46,080 GPU-hrs | Network egress | Shortest term |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nebius | Gold | $7.15 | $329,472 | Free | Hourly |
| Together AI (31–90d reserved) | Silver | $7.79 | $358,963 | Not published | 31 days |
| Together AI (on-demand) | Silver | $8.19 | $377,395 | Not published | Hourly |
| CoreWeave | Platinum | $8.60 | $396,288 | Free | Rarely short-term |
| Lambda 1-Click Cluster (64 GPU) | Silver | $9.36 | $431,309 | Free | 2 weeks |
| AWS p6-b200.48xlarge | Silver | $14.24 | $656,254 | $0.09/GB tiered | Non-cancellable block |
| Google Cloud a4-highgpu-8g | Silver | $16.11 | $742,349 | Paid | Reservation, Spot or Flex-start |

Sources, in order: Nebius lists HGX B200 at $7.15/GPU/hr on-demand and $3.95 preemptible. Together AI publishes a rare public reserved ladder — $8.19 on-demand, $7.99 at 7–30 days, $7.79 at 31–90 days, $6.79 at 91–180 days. CoreWeave lists HGX B200 at $68.80 per 8-GPU node, which is $8.60 per GPU. Lambda charges $9.86 at 16 GPUs, $9.36 at 64, $8.87 at 256+. AWS's p6-b200.48xlarge carries 8 B200s at $113.933/hour. Google's a4-highgpu-8g is $128.88/hour, or $16.11/GPU — a figure that source itself labels "on-demand-equivalent," because Google's own documentation states that for A4 machine types you must reserve capacity, use Spot VMs, use Flex-start VMs, or create a resize request in a MIG. There is no plain on-demand path to that rate. Trackers disagree wildly on this row — some publish an a4-highgpu-8g rate near $35–40/hour — but those figures imply a B200 node costing less than half Google's own prior-generation a3-highgpu-8g, which the same source puts at $87.83/hour for eight H100s. A Blackwell node at half the price of a Hopper node is not credible list pricing; $128.88 is the figure consistent with the generational step.

...

Nebius wins on price at every generation and it is not a discount-brand tradeoff: ClusterMAX rates it Gold, above Lambda, Together, AWS and Google Cloud.

Its price list is the cheapest here for H100 ($3.85), H200 ($4.50), B200 ($7.15) and B300 ($7.85), with preemptible rates roughly 45% lower and shared filesystem storage at $0.08/GiB-month. Network egress is free; note that its object storage is not — that carries a separate $0.015/GiB egress charge, which is the kind of line item that only shows up on the invoice. The Nebius review credits a Kubernetes-native platform delivering "bare-metal-equivalent performance," a managed Slurm service "completely set up and ready for use out of the box," and notes "There is no other Neocloud as open and transparent with their development as Nebius."

...

### Which GPU cloud is cheapest for training in 2026?

Nebius, at every current generation. As of 30 August 2026 its published on-demand rates are $3.85 per H100-hour, $4.50 per H200, $7.15 per B200 and $7.85 per B300, with preemptible instances about 45% cheaper and free network egress. It also holds a Gold ClusterMAX rating — above Lambda, Together, AWS and Google Cloud — so it is not a quality tradeoff. The open risks are its unsettled credit rating and colocation supply.

Which big GPU cloud is cheapest for H100 and B200? On each provider's own pricing page on November 3, 2026: for the H100, Crusoe at $3.90 per GPU-hour on demand, with Lambda a cent behind at $3.99 on an 8-GPU instance. For the B200, Lambda at $6.69 per GPU-hour (8x), well under Nebius ($8.50) and CoreWeave ($8.60). CoreWeave is the most expensive on demand, but if your job can be interrupted its published spot prices ($2.46 an H100, $4.26 a B200, per GPU) undercut everyone's on-demand rate. Two dates to know: Crusoe's own page says its H100 goes to $4.50 on December 1, 2026, which hands the cheapest on-demand H100 to Lambda.
